WhatItBlocks: Every Indian server, phone and PC. DRAM rose ~70% in one quarter and Indian assemblers absorbed it.
CoreTechnology: Sub-20nm DRAM cell capacitor and high-aspect-ratio 3D NAND channel etch
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: A 1a/1b-node DRAM cell is a capacitor of roughly 0.002 square microns at aspect ratios past 100:1, holding charge against a leakage budget measured in femtoamps. 3D NAND stacks 200-plus word-line layers and etches a channel hole through all of them in one pass. HBM adds through-silicon vias at about 10 micron pitch and, now, hybrid bonding.
WhyItIsHard: Yield at those aspect ratios is a decade of process learning that cannot be purchased. The etch and deposition recipes, not the tools, are the intellectual property, and three firms hold them.
WhereIndiaStands: Zero at cell level. Micron Sanand assembles and tests imported wafers. No Indian DRAM or NAND process exists at any node, and no programme is attempting one.

WhatItBlocks: India assembles tens of millions of air conditioners and refrigerators and imported essentially every compressor until Atomberg Innovation launched an India-designed 1.5T rotary unit in 2026. Scroll, screw, centrifugal and CO2 classes remain fully imported.
CoreTechnology: Rotary and scroll compressor rotor-profile geometry and clearance control
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: A rotary compressor runs vane and roller clearances of three to five microns across its whole temperature range. A scroll needs involute wraps held to a few microns over a 100mm spiral, with the two halves thermally matched so they stay matched hot.
WhyItIsHard: The profile is a proprietary curve tuned over decades against refrigerant, oil and noise. Harder still is grinding and pairing it in millions of units at a price an appliance bill of materials can carry.
WhereIndiaStands: Atomberg Innovation launched an India-designed 1.5-tonne rotary unit in 2026 — the first Indian rotary profile. Scroll, screw, centrifugal and CO2 transcritical classes have no Indian design at all.

HeldBy: China (80%+ of world supply, under export control)
WhatItBlocks: Every Indian machine shop, auto plant and aerospace supplier — consumables, not projects.
CoreTechnology: Tungsten APT-to-carbide conversion with grain-size inhibition
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: Ammonium paratungstate is reduced to tungsten metal powder and carburised. Submicron and ultrafine grades of 0.2 to 0.5 microns, with vanadium and chromium carbide grain-growth inhibitors, set the hardness and toughness of every cutting insert.
WhyItIsHard: Grain-size distribution and cobalt binder wetting are furnace-atmosphere crafts. The binding constraint is upstream: China holds both the ore and the conversion capacity, and has placed it under export control.
WhereIndiaStands: No primary tungsten mining at scale and no APT conversion. Cumi and Kennametal India press and sinter imported powder. Midwest Advanced and Hindustan Copper work adjacent minerals, not tungsten.

WhatItBlocks: Indian EV motor production directly.
CoreTechnology: NdFeB grain-boundary diffusion of heavy rare earths
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: A sintered magnet that holds coercivity at 150 to 180 degrees inside a traction motor needs dysprosium or terbium placed at the grain boundaries by diffusion rather than alloyed through the bulk. That single process cut heavy rare-earth content by around 80 percent while raising coercivity.
WhyItIsHard: Strip casting, hydrogen decrepitation, jet milling to single-crystal particles, aligned pressing and grain-boundary diffusion form one unbroken chain, every link of it Chinese or Japanese process knowledge. The separated dysprosium and terbium feed is itself export-controlled.
WhereIndiaStands: IREL mines and separates some light rare earths. No Indian firm makes a sintered NdFeB magnet at motor grade. Midwest Advanced and a handful of pilot lines sit at feedstock stage.

WhatItBlocks: Every Indian EV. The two most advanced Indian cell programmes run on Chinese licences.
CoreTechnology: Cathode active material synthesis and electrode calendering
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: NMC and LFP precursors are co-precipitated at controlled pH to a target particle morphology, then coated and calendered to a porosity held within a few percent along a web a kilometre long, in a dry room.
WhyItIsHard: Cell performance is set by powder morphology and electrode microstructure, not by the chemistry written on paper. The recipes and the dry-room discipline are the moat; separator and electrolyte formulation sit immediately beside them.
WhereIndiaStands: Ola and Reliance run licensed cell designs. Epsilon Carbon makes graphite anode material and Altmin has an LFP cathode pilot — both real, both small. No Indian cell at scale uses Indian cathode material.

WhatItBlocks: Medha builds world-class traction systems around imported switches.
CoreTechnology: Silicon carbide epitaxy and gate-oxide reliability on 4H-SiC
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: 150 and 200mm 4H-SiC boules grown by physical vapour transport with micropipe densities low enough to yield, then epitaxial drift layers, then a gate oxide on silicon carbide that survives twenty years in the field. On the IGBT side it is thin-wafer handling at 60 to 70 microns with field-stop implants.
WhyItIsHard: Boule growth is slow and defect-limited. The silicon-carbide-to-oxide interface, where trap density decides whether a MOSFET is good, is fixed by proprietary nitridation chemistry.
WhereIndiaStands: SiCSem is building India's first silicon carbide fab in Odisha. CDIL and Polymatech package discretes. Medha builds world-class traction inverters around entirely imported modules.

WhatItBlocks: India's pharma export industry validates every batch on imported instruments.
CoreTechnology: Quadrupole and orbitrap mass analyser machining and ion optics
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Hyperbolic quadrupole rods and orbitrap electrodes held to sub-micron form error over 200mm, driven by radio-frequency supplies stable to parts per million, inside a vacuum and ion-transfer train that is the real instrument.
WhyItIsHard: Resolution falls straight out of mechanical form error and electronics noise floor. On top sits decades of validated method libraries that regulators already accept.
WhereIndiaStands: Transasia, Agappe and Analytical Technologies build immunoassay and clinical chemistry analysers. There is no Indian mass spectrometer. India's pharma export industry validates every batch on imported instruments.

WhatItBlocks: India's entire fabless sector, regardless of ownership or funding.
CoreTechnology: Timing-closure place-and-route engines calibrated to foundry PDKs
TechnologyClassMeaning: Algorithms plus a validated model library plus an ecosystem that assumes it. The code is the small part.
WhatItActuallyIs: The product is not the editor but the optimisation engines: static timing analysis signed off against foundry-certified device models, placement and routing aware of signal integrity and on-chip variation, and design-rule decks maintained node by node.
WhyItIsHard: A tool is only usable if the foundry certifies it, and certification comes from co-development with TSMC, Samsung and Intel over years. That relationship, not the algorithms, is the lock.
WhereIndiaStands: C-DAC, InCore and Mindgrove design real silicon on licensed Synopsys and Cadence flows. There is no Indian commercial place-and-route or timing tool.

WhatItBlocks: Dholera and every Indian fab. 90%+ of equipment imported.
RecursIn: ASML · Zeiss · Atlas Copco · SK hynix
CoreTechnology: EUV plasma source and all-reflective projection optics
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: 13.5nm light from a tin droplet struck by a laser fifty thousand times a second, collected by molybdenum-silicon multilayer mirrors figured to around fifty picometres RMS, in a vacuum column whose wafer stage accelerates at thirty g and positions to below a nanometre.
WhyItIsHard: Zeiss mirror figuring and ASML's source and stage integration are two of the hardest manufacturing problems anywhere. The supply chain is single-sourced at every tier and export-controlled at state level.
WhereIndiaStands: None, and none plausible this decade. HHV builds vacuum and thin-film systems; RRCAT does precision optics research. The useful Indian question is subsystems, not scanners.

HeldBy: MAN, Wärtsilä, WinGD, GE, Safran, RR
WhatItBlocks: Indian merchant shipbuilding and every indigenous fighter airframe.
RecursIn: HD Hyundai · Imabari · RTX · Airbus · Rolls-Royce
CoreTechnology: Two-stroke crosshead marine engine design and large-bore combustion
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: Low-speed two-stroke crosshead engines above 80 megawatts with uniflow scavenging, electronically controlled common-rail injection and now dual-fuel LNG and methanol combustion control.
WhyItIsHard: The design licence, the worldwide service network and the type-approval record are the business. Crankshafts and castings at that scale have very few suppliers anywhere.
WhereIndiaStands: Kirloskar Oil Engines, Greaves and Cummins India build medium and high-speed engines competently. Indian yards licence-build MAN and Wartsila designs. No Indian large-bore design exists.

WhatItBlocks: Indian pharma plants — import alerts have shut facilities. ~31% of exports go to the US.
CoreTechnology: Regulatory data exclusivity and GMP inspection authority
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: Not a technology. The control point is the approval pathway, the inspection regime and the data packages that decide whether a product can be sold in the markets that pay.
WhyItIsHard: Nothing technical. It is the accumulated standing of a regulator, which other regulators and buyers choose to recognise.
WhereIndiaStands: CDSCO is not a reference regulator for most export markets, so Indian manufacturers design to FDA and EMA instead. Serum Institute and Bharat Biotech carry WHO prequalification, which is the closest Indian analogue.

WhatItBlocks: Every Indian-assembled phone and security camera. India makes the module; the sensor die is foreign.
CoreTechnology: Stacked backside-illuminated pixel with deep trench isolation
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Backside-illuminated pixels under one micron with deep trench isolation, on-chip colour filter and microlens, wafer-bonded to a logic die and increasingly to a DRAM layer as well. The pixel process is a specialty flow, not a logic shrink.
WhyItIsHard: Full-well capacity, dark current and crosstalk at sub-micron pitch come out of a dedicated pixel process developed over twenty years. Sony also holds the wafer-bonding and stacking recipes.
WhereIndiaStands: None. Indian camera-module assembly at Dixon and Sahasra uses imported sensors. No Indian pixel design and no Indian pixel process.

HeldBy: Dolby, Access Advance, Via LA, MPEG LA pools
WhatItBlocks: Every Indian-made phone, TV, set-top box and now car pays a per-unit royalty. No factory can fix it — the dependency is legal.
CoreTechnology: Patent pools over block-based transform coding
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: What is licensed is the toolset inside HEVC, AV1 and Dolby Atmos — motion compensation, transform and quantisation, entropy coding — claimed across thousands of patents held in several competing pools.
WhyItIsHard: The technology is published in the standard. The control is the pool and the royalty levied on every device shipped.
WhereIndiaStands: Ittiam and Amagi build codec implementations and broadcast stacks at world class, implementing standards other people own. No Indian-originated codec sits inside a shipping standard.

HeldBy: Panasonic, Mitsubishi Gas Chemical, Fuji, ASM
WhatItBlocks: The PCB capacity India is building right now, and every EMS line already running.
CoreTechnology: Low-loss laminate resin systems and chip-shooter placement accuracy
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: Copper-clad laminate is a glass-cloth and resin composite with controlled dielectric constant and loss, glass transition temperature and thermal expansion. The hard part is resin chemistry and impregnation uniformity. Alongside it, placement heads that put down a hundred thousand components an hour within 25 microns.
WhyItIsHard: Laminate is a chemistry and web-handling craft tied to the resin supplier. Placement machines are precision mechatronics where vision and feeder reliability, not speed on a datasheet, decide the purchase.
WhereIndiaStands: Ascent Circuits and Kaynes Circuits fabricate boards on imported laminate. No Indian laminate maker at electronics grade and no Indian placement machine.

WhatItBlocks: Every Indian analog and mixed-signal startup designs in tools and licenses cells it cannot substitute.
CoreTechnology: Precision analog topology and silicon-proven foundation IP libraries
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: Bandgap references, phase-locked loops, SerDes, converters and the standard-cell and memory-compiler libraries every system-on-chip is assembled from, each characterised per foundry node across process, voltage and temperature.
WhyItIsHard: Analog does not scale with nodes. It is designer-years of layout-dependent-effect knowledge plus silicon-proven characterisation, and a library business needs a standing foundry relationship.
WhereIndiaStands: FermionIC, Signalchip, Vervesemi, Netrasemi and SmartSoC build genuine analog and mixed-signal IP. This is India's strongest semiconductor position. There is still no Indian foundation-IP library at Artisan scale.

WhatItBlocks: Every Indian air purifier and vacuum uses imported media — a consumable, sold repeatedly.
CoreTechnology: Wet-laid microglass media and durable meltblown electret charging
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: HEPA media is a wet-laid web of sub-micron borosilicate glass fibres at controlled basis weight and pore structure. The cheaper route is meltblown polypropylene given an electrostatic charge that has to survive humidity and years of service.
WhyItIsHard: Drawing fibre to sub-micron, forming a uniform web, and making the charge durable are the technology. Pleating and sealing a pack without a single leak path is the other half.
WhereIndiaStands: Bry-Air, Praan and a long list of assemblers convert imported media competently. No Indian HEPA media production at all.

WhatItBlocks: India is building six-plus fabs and OSATs and imports ~90% of the equipment, including the precision subassemblies inside it.
CoreTechnology: Ultra-high-vacuum chamber fabrication and particle-free surface finishing
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Chambers, gas panels, electrostatic chucks and frames built to ultra-high-vacuum standards: electropolished surfaces, ultra-clean welding, leak rates below 1e-10 mbar-litres per second, assembled inside cleanrooms.
WhyItIsHard: No exotic physics. What is hard is a quality system an original equipment maker will audit and qualify, which takes years and a reference customer.
WhereIndiaStands: HHV genuinely builds vacuum systems. Godrej, MTAR and Aequs have the machining and the cleanroom discipline. This is an opening blocked by qualification, not by capability.

WhatItBlocks: Die attach, underfills and encapsulants physically hold every packaged chip together. India is building OSATs and importing all of it.
CoreTechnology: Die-attach, underfill and moulding compound formulation at electronic grade
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: Epoxy moulding compounds, capillary underfills, die-attach films and dicing tapes with controlled thermal expansion, ionic purity below parts per billion and cure kinetics matched to a specific package.
WhyItIsHard: Purity and filler dispersion at electronic grade, then a qualification that runs for years per package family. Nobody risks a new supplier on a shipping product.
WhereIndiaStands: Anabond, Pidilite and Resinova make capable industrial adhesives, none at semiconductor grade. Tata Electronics, CG Semi and Kaynes Semicon will import every one of these materials.

HeldBy: Shin-Etsu, SUMCO, GlobalWafers, Siltronic, SK Siltron
WhatItBlocks: Every chip starts on one. India is building fabs and will import every wafer.
RecursIn: SK Group · ASML · Samsung · Tata Electronics
CoreTechnology: Czochralski 300mm crystal pulling with controlled oxygen and defect density
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: 300mm boules pulled under a magnetic field with interstitial oxygen, resistivity and crystal-originated pit density inside narrow windows, then wire-sawn, lapped, etched, double-side polished and epitaxially coated to nanometre flatness.
WhyItIsHard: Crystal pulling is thermal-field control learned over decades. Wafer flatness and nanotopography specifications are tighter than the lithography that will be printed on them.
WhereIndiaStands: None at 300mm, and no polysilicon feedstock either. A few proposals exist on paper. Every Indian fab plan imports its substrate.

HeldBy: Asahi Kasei, Toray, SK ie technology, Senior
WhatItBlocks: Separator film determines cell safety; a hard polymer process behind every Indian cell programme.
CoreTechnology: Wet-process polyolefin film stretching and ceramic coating
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Ultra-high molecular weight polyethylene dissolved in oil, cast, biaxially stretched and extracted to leave a 7 to 16 micron film at around 40 percent porosity with sub-100nm pores, then ceramic-coated for thermal shutdown.
WhyItIsHard: The extraction and stretch schedule set the pore structure. Defect tolerance is effectively zero, because a pinhole in a separator is a cell fire.
WhereIndiaStands: None in production. Gujarat Fluorochemicals, SRF and Cosmo Films hold genuinely adjacent film capability. This is a capital and qualification gap, not a physics one.

HeldBy: JSR, TOK, Shin-Etsu, Fujifilm, Sumitomo, Merck
WhatItBlocks: Consumed continuously by every wafer. India imports 85-90% of fab chemicals with no domestic fallback.
CoreTechnology: ArF and EUV resist polymer synthesis and photoacid generator chemistry
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: A resist is a matrix polymer, a photoacid generator and a quencher tuned to trade resolution, line-edge roughness and sensitivity against each other, with metal-ion purity below parts per billion. EUV resists add stochastic defect physics on top.
WhyItIsHard: Polymer synthesis plus metal-ion control plus a qualification cycle measured in years for every node. The trade-off triangle has no free corner.
WhereIndiaStands: Nothing at semiconductor grade. Navin Fluorine, Deepak Nitrite, SRF and Gujarat Fluorochemicals already make the fluorochemistry next door to it. This is the clearest capital-and-qualification opening in Indian chemicals.

HeldBy: Fujifilm and Sony — the only two makers worldwide
WhatItBlocks: Archival storage for every hyperscaler, and growing on AI data retention. No Indian adjacency exists.
CoreTechnology: Barium ferrite particulate coating and servo writing
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: Sub-50nm barium or strontium ferrite particles dispersed and coated onto a polyester web to nanometre thickness uniformity, then servo-written so a head can track a path a micron wide along a kilometre of half-inch tape.
WhyItIsHard: Particle synthesis, dispersion, web coating and head-media co-design, qualified by a consortium that controls the format. Only Fujifilm and Sony have ever done it.
WhereIndiaStands: None. Cosmo Films and Jindal Poly Films coat polyester film at industrial scale, which is a long way from magnetic grade. Every Indian archive runs on imported tape.

WhatItBlocks: The polariser film under every LCD panel — a second layer behind the display fab gap.
CoreTechnology: Solution-cast cellulose triacetate and stretched optical compensation film
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: Triacetate film solution-cast to optical clarity with controlled retardation, plus stretched cyclo-olefin or acrylic compensation layers either side of an iodine-stained polyvinyl alcohol polariser.
WhyItIsHard: Solution casting at optical grade across a wide web with no defects, and retardation held to specification. The retardation control is the real intellectual property.
WhereIndiaStands: None. Indian display module assembly imports the complete polariser stack, which is a material share of a panel's cost.

HeldBy: Canon (industry standard), ASML, Veeco, SUSS MicroTec
WhatItBlocks: India is building OSATs at Sanand and Jagiroad and will import every back-end stepper.
CoreTechnology: Large-field 1:1 projection steppers for panel-level packaging
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: i-line steppers with fields far larger than front-end tools, telecentric optics, and focus tracking across substrates that warp as they cure, resolving one to two micron redistribution lines on reconstituted wafers and panels.
WhyItIsHard: Optics over a very large field, plus overlay on a substrate that moves during exposure. Canon's installed base effectively defines the process window the industry designs to.
WhereIndiaStands: None. Tata's Assam assembly plant and Kaynes Semicon will buy these tools, as will every Indian packaging line that follows.

WhatItBlocks: Every advanced chip on earth is made by one company. India's Dholera fab targets 28nm and above on licensed process technology.
CoreTechnology: Gate-all-around transistor integration and defect-density learning
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Nanosheet gate-all-around transistors with inner spacers, dipole work-function tuning and buried power rails, patterned by EUV multipatterning — and the defect-density learning curve that turns a working process into a profitable yield.
WhyItIsHard: Thousands of steps co-optimised, where the rate of learning is the actual product. Leading edge is not licensable: TSMC, Samsung and Intel do not license it at any price.
WhereIndiaStands: Tata Electronics' Dholera fab targets 28nm on PSMC technology. That is a real and useful fab. The distance to leading edge is generational, and closing it needs process R&D, not another fab.

WhatItBlocks: The binding constraint on every AI accelerator shipped. India is building conventional OSAT a generation behind.
CoreTechnology: Silicon interposer through-via formation and hybrid bonding
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: A silicon interposer carrying through-silicon vias and fine-pitch redistribution, holding HBM stacks beside a logic die. Newer flows drop the microbumps and bond copper directly to copper at sub-10 micron pitch.
WhyItIsHard: Warpage control across a very large module, through-via reveal, and bonding surfaces flat to a few nanometres across 300mm. Capacity here, not wafer capacity, has been the binding constraint on AI silicon.
WhereIndiaStands: Tata Semiconductor Assembly and Test, Kaynes Semicon, CG Semi and Micron Sanand are building conventional assembly and test. No Indian interposer and no hybrid bonding.

WhatItBlocks: Every fab layer needs a mask. India has no mask shop and none is announced.
CoreTechnology: Electron-beam mask writing and defect repair on quartz
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Multi-beam electron-beam writers patterning chrome or molybdenum-silicide films on quartz, then inspection at sensitivities finer than the feature that will print, then repair by focused ion or electron beam.
WhyItIsHard: Placement accuracy below a nanometre, write times that decide economics, and delivery of a mask with no printable defect. Mask shops live inside the foundry's qualification system.
WhereIndiaStands: None. A 28nm fab needs a mask supply chain that India does not have, which makes every mask set an import with a lead time.

HeldBy: Picanol, Toyota Industries, Tsudakoma, Itema, Dornier
WhatItBlocks: India is the world's second-largest textile producer and weaves on imported looms.
CoreTechnology: Air-jet weft insertion above a thousand picks per minute
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Relay nozzles timed to microseconds carry a weft across 1.9 metres more than a thousand times a minute, with electronic dobby or jacquard shedding and closed-loop let-off and take-up.
WhyItIsHard: The insertion physics, and then reliability for a machine expected to run continuously for a decade. The service network weighs as heavily as the specification.
WhereIndiaStands: Lakshmi Machine Works and Trumac build spinning machinery at world class — proof the engineering base exists. Indian weaving machines are rapier and projectile at lower speed. The nearest Indian firms to a real attempt.

WhatItBlocks: Losing the Android licence stalled Huawei as hard as losing EDA. BharOS is India's only equivalent effort.
CoreTechnology: Application framework, driver model and app-store trust chain
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: The kernel is open. The control is the hardware abstraction and driver model, the compatibility test suite, the bundled services and the signing and trust chain that developers and manufacturers build against.
WhyItIsHard: The technology is reproducible and has been reproduced. The barrier is the application ecosystem and the certification an OEM needs to ship.
WhereIndiaStands: BharOS from IIT Madras and Indus OS both exist and work. Every Indian handset maker ships Android. This is decision and ecosystem, not capability.

HeldBy: NVIDIA (overwhelming majority of AI training silicon)
WhatItBlocks: India's entire AI compute build-out is procurement of one company's hardware, under US export licensing. The H20 episode cost NVIDIA $4.5bn and showed allocation is a policy instrument.
RecursIn: NVIDIA · Amazon · Dell · HPE · SK hynix
CoreTechnology: Tensor-core microarchitecture plus a mature compiler and kernel stack
TechnologyClassMeaning: Algorithms plus a validated model library plus an ecosystem that assumes it. The code is the small part.
WhatItActuallyIs: The silicon is a systolic matrix-multiply array with a memory hierarchy tuned around it. The moat is CUDA — cuDNN, cuBLAS, NCCL, the compiler, and every framework's fast path assuming all of it.
WhyItIsHard: Software maturity measured in years of kernel tuning by people who also designed the hardware. Then HBM supply and advanced-packaging allocation, both of which are rationed.
WhereIndiaStands: C-DAC's accelerator work and the Neysa and QpiAI programmes are early but real. India runs substantial GPU cloud capacity at Yotta, Neysa and E2E on entirely imported silicon.

Chokepoint: Fab process equipment (deposition, etch, implant, CMP)
HeldBy: Applied Materials, Lam Research, Tokyo Electron, KLA
WhatItBlocks: Where ASML holds patterning, these four hold everything else. India's fabs import the whole tool set.
RecursIn: Applied Materials · ASML · Atlas Copco · Samsung
CoreTechnology: Atomic-layer deposition conformality and high-aspect-ratio plasma etch
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Self-limiting deposition cycles giving angstrom-level conformality inside structures a hundred times deeper than they are wide, and plasma etch with pulsed sources and endpoint detection that stops on films a few nanometres thick.
WhyItIsHard: Chamber design and plasma uniformity, then a recipe library co-developed with chipmakers over a decade. The recipe, not the chamber, is what is being sold.
WhereIndiaStands: HHV builds deposition and vacuum systems for research and specialty production, which is a genuine base to grow from. Nothing yet at production semiconductor grade.

HeldBy: Seagate, Western Digital, Toshiba — three suppliers worldwide
WhatItBlocks: The storage layer under every hyperscale data centre. India is building data centres at scale and has no HDD capability at drive, head or media level.
RecursIn: Western Digital · Dell · HPE · NTT · Amazon
CoreTechnology: Magnetic recording head fabrication and granular media stack
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: A head with a tunnelling magnetoresistive reader and, for heat-assisted recording, a plasmonic near-field transducer and laser diode at the pole tip, flying about a nanometre above a granular iron-platinum media layer on a glass substrate.
WhyItIsHard: Head wafers are fabricated to semiconductor standards, and near-field transducer reliability at temperature is still the hardest open problem in storage. Three suppliers remain, and the number is falling.
WhereIndiaStands: None. India buys nearline storage for every data centre it builds, and the data-centre build-out is one of its fastest growing industries.

HeldBy: Ibiden, Shinko, Unimicron, Nan Ya PCB, AT&S
WhatItBlocks: The mini-PCB inside every chip package, and the AI packaging bottleneck. India's OSATs will import every one.
CoreTechnology: Build-up film lamination and semi-additive fine-line plating
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: Package substrates with laser-drilled microvias and semi-additive plated lines below ten microns, laminated with Ajinomoto build-up film on a coreless or glass core.
WhyItIsHard: Warpage, plating uniformity and yield across large body sizes. The film itself has effectively one supplier, which has repeatedly been the industry's tightest constraint.
WhereIndiaStands: None. This is the quiet constraint under every Indian assembly and test plan, and it is rarely named in the policy documents.

HeldBy: Qualcomm, MediaTek, Apple, Samsung LSI, UNISOC
WhatItBlocks: India assembles the world's phones and designs none of the silicon inside them.
CoreTechnology: Modem and SoC integration with worldwide carrier certification
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: A CPU cluster, GPU, neural engine and image signal processor integrated with a cellular modem, taped out at leading edge, then certified across carriers and bands in every market the phone will sell in.
WhyItIsHard: The modem and its field-proven protocol stack, plus the certification burden — not the CPU cores, which are licensable.
WhereIndiaStands: Signalchip built India's first 4G and 5G modem silicon. Saankhya, now inside Tejas, and WiSig build 5G and narrowband IoT chips. No Indian application processor is in a shipping phone.

WhatItBlocks: A per-unit royalty on every handset India makes. Indian manufacturers have lost SEP litigation in Indian courts.
CoreTechnology: Channel coding and massive MIMO inside 3GPP releases
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: LDPC and polar coding, massive-MIMO beamforming and retransmission procedures standardised through 3GPP and claimed across thousands of declared patents, licensed per handset.
WhyItIsHard: Decades of standards participation, with engineers in the room when the technique is chosen. The engineering is published; the royalty position is not.
WhereIndiaStands: Tejas Networks, Saankhya, WiSig and CEWiT contributed to 5Gi and to 3GPP and hold some declared patents. India remains a substantial net payer of cellular royalties.

WhatItBlocks: India is the world's second-largest cement producer and imports full-line plant technology.
RecursIn: Haldor Topsoe group · SMS & Danieli · Sandvik
CoreTechnology: Pyroprocessing kiln design and vertical roller mill geometry
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: Preheater and precalciner towers, kiln burner and clinker cooler design backed by heat and gas-flow models, plus vertical roller mills whose table and roller geometry set kilowatt-hours per tonne of cement.
WhyItIsHard: Process models validated across hundreds of operating plants. What is actually sold is a guarantee on specific energy consumption, and only a long reference list supports one.
WhereIndiaStands: ISGEC, Walchandnagar, Thermax and Elecon supply components and some plant scope, and L&T has the engineering. Indian cement groups still buy FLSmidth and thyssenkrupp pyro lines.

WhatItBlocks: India is among the world's largest grain, pulse and milk producers and imports the processing plant.
RecursIn: John Deere group · Bühler group · Alfa Laval · Tetra Pak group
CoreTechnology: Roller mill flute geometry, milling diagrams and optical sorting
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: Chilled-iron roller mills with specific flute geometry and differential speeds, plansifters and purifiers — and sorters using hyperspectral or CCD imaging with ejection valves firing in milliseconds.
WhyItIsHard: The milling diagram, meaning the sequence and settings for each grain and each flour specification, is proprietary process knowledge. Sorter accuracy is optics plus a trained classifier.
WhereIndiaStands: Nichrome, Praj and a number of mill builders equip domestic plants capably. Buhler and Satake hold the premium flour and rice lines. One of the strongest adjacencies in the ledger.

WhatItBlocks: India supplies a fifth of the world's generics and imports most of the high-speed blister, cartoning and aseptic filling lines.
CoreTechnology: Serialised high-speed blister and isolator filling line integration
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Blister formers, cartoners and isolator-based aseptic fillers running at hundreds of units a minute with vision inspection, serialisation and validated changeover, documented end to end under GAMP.
WhyItIsHard: Mechanical reliability at speed, and then the validation package and track record that regulators and auditors accept without argument.
WhereIndiaStands: India is the world's largest generic manufacturer and buys IMA, Syntegon and Uhlmann lines. Indian machine builders serve domestic lines well. The export-grade serialised isolator class is the gap.

HeldBy: ASM International, BESI, Applied Materials, Tokyo Electron
WhatItBlocks: ALD, die attach and hybrid bonding — the tools India's fabs and OSATs will buy first.
RecursIn: ASM & BESI · Applied Materials · ASE · Canon
CoreTechnology: Flip-chip bonder placement accuracy and thermocompression control
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Die bonders placing to one to three microns with force and temperature profiles for thermocompression, and increasingly hybrid bonding at sub-micron overlay, inside a clean and vibration-isolated frame.
WhyItIsHard: Precision mechatronics plus bond-process physics. The installed tool base defines what recipe an assembly plant can run at all.
WhereIndiaStands: None. India's assembly and test build-out is entirely a tool import, which is the part of the semiconductor mission with no domestic supply plan.

HeldBy: IMAX, Dolby Cinema, CJ 4DPLEX; Barco, Christie, NEC on projectors
WhatItBlocks: India makes more films than any country and licenses every premium exhibition format and every projector.
CoreTechnology: Laser projection light engines and object-based audio rendering
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: RGB laser illumination with speckle management driving high-contrast digital micromirror or LCoS imaging, plus object-based audio rendered to a specific room layout by a licensed processor.
WhyItIsHard: The format licence and the certified auditorium, rather more than the optics. A screen is sold on the brand above the door.
WhereIndiaStands: PVR INOX, Miraj and Prasad EFX operate and service at scale, and DNEG and Prime Focus do world-class post-production. No Indian projector and no Indian premium format.

WhatItBlocks: India is the world's largest milk producer and every aseptic carton line is imported.
RecursIn: Tetra Pak group · Bühler group · Nestlé
CoreTechnology: Peroxide-sterilised web forming and barrier carton laminate
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: A paper, aluminium and polymer laminate sterilised in hydrogen peroxide, then formed, filled and sealed inside a sterile tunnel at hundreds of packs a minute — plus the laminate itself.
WhyItIsHard: Sterility assurance validated machine by machine, and a barrier layer that holds ambient shelf life for months. The razor-and-blade tie between filler and packaging material is the commercial lock.
WhereIndiaStands: Nichrome and several Indian fillers serve domestic FMCG. Amul and Parle buy Tetra Pak systems. No Indian aseptic laminate at that barrier class.

HeldBy: GE Aerospace, Pratt & Whitney, Rolls-Royce, Safran via CFM
WhatItBlocks: Hot-section metallurgy and single-crystal blades. Kaveri ran forty years and failed; India makes the parts and not the engine.
RecursIn: Boeing & GE Aerospace · Rolls-Royce · Airbus · Doosan
CoreTechnology: Single-crystal turbine blade casting and thermal barrier coatings
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Hot-section blades cast as single crystals in directionally solidified nickel superalloy, cooling passages formed by ceramic cores, coated by electron-beam physical vapour deposition, and run in gas hotter than the alloy's own melting point.
WhyItIsHard: Casting yield, core technology and coating life, on top of full-authority control and certification. The hot section is why no new entrant has succeeded in fifty years.
WhereIndiaStands: Azad Engineering, MTAR, Aequs and Bharat Forge supply hot-section parts to GE, Safran and Rolls-Royce — real capability inside somebody else's design. GTRE's Kaveri never cleared the hot section; HAL licence-builds.

WhatItBlocks: VA Tech Wabag builds world-class plants around imported membranes.
CoreTechnology: Interfacial polymerisation of thin-film composite polyamide
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: A rejection layer around a hundred nanometres thick formed by interfacial polymerisation on a polysulfone support, then spiral-wound with feed spacers. Salt rejection and fouling resistance come out of that film's chemistry.
WhyItIsHard: Monomer chemistry and post-treatment, plus casting a support with no defects and winding an element with no leak. Narrower than most gaps in this ledger.
WhereIndiaStands: Permionics and Ion Exchange make membranes and plants, and VA Tech Wabag does the engineering at world scale. Indian plants still buy DuPont and Toray elements.

HeldBy: John Deere, Trimble, Topcon, AGCO PTx
WhatItBlocks: India makes more tractors than anyone and none of the guidance and variable-rate systems that carry the margin.
CoreTechnology: RTK correction networks fused with ISOBUS machine control
TechnologyClassMeaning: Algorithms plus a validated model library plus an ecosystem that assumes it. The code is the small part.
WhatItActuallyIs: Centimetre positioning from real-time kinematic base networks, fused with implement control over ISOBUS, section control, and agronomic models built on several seasons of field data.
WhyItIsHard: The data and the installed fleet. The radios and receivers are close to commodity; the model trained on a million hectares is not.
WhereIndiaStands: TAFE, Sonalika, VST Tillers, Escorts and Mahindra build tractors at world scale, and Cropin and Fasal write good agronomic software. The gap is the machine-control and data layer between them.

WhatItBlocks: The largest single input cost in paint and coatings, and India imports most of it against sub-scale domestic producers.
CoreTechnology: Chloride-route TiO2 and rutile surface treatment
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Ilmenite or rutile chlorinated to titanium tetrachloride, oxidised to pigment-grade TiO2, then surface-treated with alumina and silica for durability and dispersion, with particle size held near 250 nanometres for opacity.
WhyItIsHard: The chloride route's corrosion engineering and chlorine recycle. Surface treatment is what separates a commodity grade from a premium one.
WhereIndiaStands: Travancore Titanium and KMML run sulphate-route plants. There is no Indian chloride-route pigment, so Asian Paints and the whole coatings industry import premium grades.

WhatItBlocks: Every chip bring-up, board qualification and materials test runs on an imported instrument. India designs a fifth of the world's chips and measures none of them on Indian equipment.
CoreTechnology: Wideband ADC front ends and traceably calibrated RF signal chains
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: Real-time oscilloscopes with multi-gigahertz front ends and interleaved converters, and vector network and signal analysers whose accuracy rests on traceable calibration and the correction mathematics behind it.
WhyItIsHard: The analog front end and its custom converter, metrological traceability, and decades of application software engineers already know how to drive.
WhereIndiaStands: Toshniwal, Systronics, Modsonic and Scientech build instruments for industry and education, and Data Patterns builds defence test equipment at genuine class. No Indian high-end scope or network analyser.

WhatItBlocks: The platform, not the tool, is the moat — and it locks a tradesman in for a decade. India assembles around imported cells, motors and controllers.
RecursIn: Techtronic Industries · Stanley Black & Decker · Makita · Bosch
CoreTechnology: Pack electronics, abuse tolerance and platform lock-in
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: 18 and 36 volt packs with cell balancing, temperature-managed fast charge and a tool-to-pack communication protocol, plus a connector that keeps a tradesman inside one brand for a decade.
WhyItIsHard: Not the cells. The pack electronics, the abuse tolerance, and above all the installed base of tools that already accept that pack.
WhereIndiaStands: Cheston, iBELL, Ralli Wolf, Xtra Power and Shakti sell cordless tools on mostly Chinese platforms. Exide, Amara Raja and Livguard can build packs today. Decision, not technology.

HeldBy: Hilti, ITW (Ramset, Red Head), fischer, Simpson Strong-Tie
WhatItBlocks: India builds at enormous scale and imports the certified structural anchors that hold it together.
CoreTechnology: Approved anchor design with seismic-qualified load tables
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: Undercut and bonded anchors whose load tables are backed by tested approvals covering cracked concrete and seismic categories, plus the design software a structural engineer specifies from.
WhyItIsHard: The approval and the software, not the steel. An anchor without an approval cannot be written into a drawing, however good it is.
WhereIndiaStands: Anabond, Resinova and MYK Laticrete serve the market, and Indian makers sell on BIS marks without European or ICC approvals. A pure qualification barrier on top of adequate product.

HeldBy: TTI (Milwaukee, Ryobi, AEG, Ridgid licence), Stanley (DEWALT, Craftsman, Irwin, Porter-Cable)
WhatItBlocks: An entrant does not face five competitors across five price tiers — it faces two owners wearing a dozen badges. Brand consolidation, not brand competition, is the barrier.
RecursIn: Techtronic Industries · Stanley Black & Decker · Chervon · Makita
CoreTechnology: Brand portfolios and channel control over commodity tool manufacture
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: The manufacturing technology is widely available and largely Chinese. The control is brand, shelf space and a battery platform, which TTI and Stanley have spent thirty years consolidating.
WhyItIsHard: Channel and brand equity. Nothing a factory can solve.
WhereIndiaStands: Groz, Taparia, Jhalani, Freemans and Pye make hand tools of real quality and export as contract manufacturers. There is no Indian power-tool brand of scale.

HeldBy: SubCom, Alcatel Submarine Networks, NEC, HMN Tech
WhatItBlocks: Three or four firms build the physical internet backbone. India lands major cables and manufactures no cable, repeaters or wet plant.
RecursIn: SubCom · Alcatel Submarine Networks · Prysmian · NTT
CoreTechnology: Pressure-qualified optical repeaters and deepwater cable armouring
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Erbium-doped fibre amplifier repeaters in beryllium-copper housings that survive 8,000 metres of depth and twenty-five years unserviced, powered down ten thousand kilometres of copper, inside a cable with steel-wire armour and polyethylene insulation.
WhyItIsHard: Twenty-five-year unattended reliability qualification. The wet plant is where all the risk lives, and no consortium will finance an unproven supplier.
WhereIndiaStands: STL and HFCL make fibre and terrestrial cable at world scale, with Birla Cable and Aksh Optifibre alongside. No Indian repeater and no wet-plant qualification. One of the clearest openings in Indian telecom hardware.

HeldBy: SubCom, Global Marine, Orange Marine, ASN, NTT WE Marine
WhatItBlocks: India owns no cable ship. Repairs to cables landing in India depend on foreign vessels under consortium agreements.
RecursIn: SubCom · Alcatel Submarine Networks · Greek shipowners · Maersk
CoreTechnology: Cable engines, dynamic positioning and at-sea jointing qualification
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Linear cable engines and drum tensioners paying out under controlled tension, DP2 and DP3 station keeping, plough burial, and splicing at sea in a jointing shack held to factory specification.
WhyItIsHard: The jointing accreditation and the crew who hold it. The vessel itself is well within what Indian yards build.
WhereIndiaStands: Cochin Shipyard, Mazagon Dock, GRSE and L&T build complex vessels, and Knowledge Marine and Ocean Sparkle operate fleets. India has no cable ship and no jointing accreditation, and repairs its own landings on foreign vessels.

HeldBy: SLB (OneSubsea, Cameron), TechnipFMC, Aker Solutions, Baker Hughes
WhatItBlocks: Deepwater trees, manifolds, umbilicals and BOPs. India operates deepwater fields and manufactures none of the hardware on the seabed.
CoreTechnology: Subsea tree and control module qualification to API 17D
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Horizontal and vertical subsea trees, manifolds and electro-hydraulic control modules qualified to API 17D and 17F for ten to fifteen thousand psi at depth, with metal-to-metal sealing and twenty-five-year retrievability.
WhyItIsHard: Qualification testing and then a place on an operator's approved vendor list, which is where the real gate sits. A global service base follows.
WhereIndiaStands: L&T builds subsea structures and has supplied manifolds, and Planys and EyeROV cover inspection. ONGC buys trees from SLB, TechnipFMC and Aker. Qualification, not technology.

WhatItBlocks: No rig gets built without this equipment. India drills at scale and manufactures none of it.
CoreTechnology: Blowout preventer ram sealing and well-control certification
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Shear and pipe rams that seal fifteen thousand psi on a moving string, with elastomer packers qualified hot and cold, certified to API 16A and carrying a documented service history.
WhyItIsHard: Certification and liability. The forging and machining is within reach of several Indian firms today.
WhereIndiaStands: Jindal Drilling and Aban operate rigs, and Bharat Forge, Godrej and L&T have the forging and machining. There is no Indian blowout preventer. Decision and qualification.

WhatItBlocks: The gating equipment on every high-rise site. ACE is India's only maker at that class and imports the control and anti-collision systems.
CoreTechnology: Mast section fatigue design and load-moment control
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: Bolted and pinned mast sections designed to published fatigue classes, slewing rings and hoist gearboxes, with load-moment limiters and anti-collision control for congested sites.
WhyItIsHard: Fatigue certification, the hire fleet behind it, and service response. The structure is ordinary steel for Indian fabricators.
WhereIndiaStands: ACE builds tower cranes, with Anupam Industries, ElectroMech, Vijay Cranes and Sanghvi Movers across lifting. Liebherr and Potain hold the tall, large-capacity class. Decision.

HeldBy: Subsea7, TechnipFMC, Saipem, Allseas, Oceaneering, McDermott
WhatItBlocks: Installing and maintaining anything on the seabed needs purpose-built vessels. India operates deepwater fields and owns none, so every intervention is contracted to a foreign fleet.
CoreTechnology: Pipelay and heavy-lift vessel systems with installation engineering
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: J-lay and S-lay towers, reel-lay systems, three-thousand-tonne cranes and DP3 vessels, plus the installation analysis that proves a lift or a lay will survive a given sea state.
WhyItIsHard: The asset base and the project record. Operators award deepwater installation on track record, which cannot be bought with one vessel.
WhereIndiaStands: L&T Offshore does offshore engineering and construction at genuine scale, with Dolphin Offshore and Shreyas on support vessels. No Indian deepwater pipelay asset.

WhatItBlocks: The gas-tight thread that makes OCTG usable in deepwater and HPHT wells. India produces pipe at world scale and licenses the connection on the end of it.
CoreTechnology: Gas-tight metal-to-metal premium threaded connection design
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: A thread form with a torque shoulder and a metal-to-metal seal that stays gas-tight through compression, bending and thermal cycling, validated to the highest ISO 13679 category.
WhyItIsHard: The proprietary geometry, the test record behind it, and the surface treatment that stops galling on makeup. A connection is sold on its qualification envelope.
WhereIndiaStands: Jindal SAW, Maharashtra Seamless and Welspun make seamless pipe at world scale and licence their connections. No Indian premium connection design — a design and qualification gap sitting on top of real pipe capability.

HeldBy: Oceaneering, Subsea7, Saab Seaeye, Forum Energy
WhatItBlocks: Intervention ROVs with manipulators, purpose-built seabed tooling and umbilicals. India now builds inspection-class ROVs commercially through Planys and EyeROV; the deepwater intervention class above them remains foreign.
CoreTechnology: Work-class ROV hydraulics, tooling interfaces and 3,000m qualification
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: 150 to 250 horsepower hydraulic vehicles with seven-function manipulators, tether management systems and tool interfaces standardised to operator practice, qualified to three thousand metres.
WhyItIsHard: Depth qualification and the surrounding tooling ecosystem. The vehicle itself is achievable for a competent Indian engineering firm.
WhereIndiaStands: Planys Technologies and EyeROV build inspection-class ROVs of real quality, with Coratia and Xera Robotics adjacent. Work-class depth is the gap: capital and qualification, not physics.

WhatItBlocks: Effectively a monopoly, paired with every lithography scanner, and inside Japan's export control regime.
RecursIn: Tokyo Electron · ASML · Applied Materials · Canon
CoreTechnology: Resist coat and develop uniformity with lithocell integration
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Track systems spinning resist to nanometre thickness uniformity, with bake plates flat to milli-kelvin and a transfer robot clocking a wafer every few seconds, mechanically and logically integrated to the scanner.
WhyItIsHard: Thermal uniformity and defect control across a tool that never stops. Tokyo Electron is effectively sole source at advanced nodes.
WhereIndiaStands: None. The track is bought with the scanner and rarely appears in any Indian equipment discussion.

HeldBy: Lam Research, Tokyo Electron, Applied Materials
WhatItBlocks: The step that physically shapes every transistor and enables 3D NAND and gate-all-around structures.
RecursIn: Lam Research · Applied Materials · Tokyo Electron · SK hynix
CoreTechnology: Pulsed-plasma source design and chamber-to-chamber matching
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Capacitively and inductively coupled sources with pulsed bias for selectivity and ion-energy control, plus the chamber matching and wall-condition management that keeps one recipe identical across fifty chambers.
WhyItIsHard: Plasma uniformity and matching. The recipe library is the real asset and it is co-owned with the customer.
WhereIndiaStands: Nothing at production grade. HHV's vacuum and plasma systems are the Indian base worth building on.

WhatItBlocks: Yield learning is what makes a fab economic rather than merely operational. India has no capability at fab class.
CoreTechnology: Optical scatterometry and e-beam inspection with model-based inversion
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Scatterometry inferring three-dimensional profiles from reflected spectra against a solved optical model, broadband inspection at sensitivities below the printed feature, electron-beam review, and the control loop that feeds corrections back into the process.
WhyItIsHard: The inverse problem and the detection physics. KLA's position rests on sensitivity plus twenty years of defect classification data.
WhereIndiaStands: None. Modsonic and Accurate Gauging do industrial non-destructive testing and gauging well, which is a different discipline entirely.

WhatItBlocks: Most of the world's data centre fabrics run on Tomahawk and Jericho class silicon. India builds the systems and none of the chips.
CoreTechnology: High-radix switch ASIC with 200G SerDes and a forwarding SDK
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: 51.2 terabit switch chips with more than a hundred 200G PAM4 SerDes lanes, shared packet buffers and a programmable forwarding pipeline, plus the software development kit every network operating system is written against.
WhyItIsHard: SerDes at 200 gigabits a lane, and then an SDK ecosystem. Broadcom's SDK is the lock, not the silicon.
WhereIndiaStands: Tejas Networks and Galore Networks build carrier and access systems on merchant silicon, and Saankhya built broadcast SoCs. No Indian switch ASIC.

WhatItBlocks: A duopoly on export-controlled parts. DRDO, ISRO and every Indian defence electronics programme designs around imported FPGAs.
CoreTechnology: LUT fabric architecture and the closed bitstream toolchain
TechnologyClassMeaning: Algorithms plus a validated model library plus an ecosystem that assumes it. The code is the small part.
WhatItActuallyIs: An array of look-up tables, DSP slices, block memory and hard IP, with a bitstream format only the vendor can generate and a synthesis and place-and-route toolchain that took a decade to make usable.
WhyItIsHard: The toolchain and the IP library far more than the fabric. A domestic FPGA without a toolchain is an unprogrammable die.
WhereIndiaStands: Nothing commercial. C-DAC, ISRO and DRDO design on Xilinx and Altera parts, and a domestic FPGA has been proposed repeatedly without a software plan.

HeldBy: Philips, GE HealthCare, Vermon, Blatek, Sonoscape
WhatItBlocks: The value-dense component in every ultrasound system. India runs the world's highest scan volumes and assembles systems around imported probes.
CoreTechnology: Piezocomposite array dicing, acoustic matching and lens lamination
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Lead zirconate titanate or single-crystal piezo diced into 128 to 256 elements at sub-millimetre pitch, with matching layers, backing and lens, flex-bonded to a beamformer. The newer route is a MEMS capacitive or piezoelectric array.
WhyItIsHard: Element-to-element uniformity, kerf filling and acoustic bonding at yield. The beamformer and image chain are the easier half.
WhereIndiaStands: Trivitron and others assemble ultrasound systems around imported probes, and Sahajanand and Meril have precision medical manufacturing. No Indian transducer array.

WhatItBlocks: The platforms Indian fabless firms in RF, power and edge AI actually need. India's fab programme targets licensed mature logic and offers none of them.
CoreTechnology: SOI substrate engineering and trap-rich RF isolation
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Silicon-on-insulator wafers with a buried oxide and a trap-rich layer that suppresses harmonic distortion for antenna switches, or fully depleted thin-film transistors with back-bias. A specialty flow, not a shrink.
WhyItIsHard: The substrate, whose layer-transfer process has one dominant supplier, and then device and process co-design. What gets delivered to a customer is a PDK.
WhereIndiaStands: None. SiCSem and the proposed compound-semiconductor fabs are the nearest intent. Indian RF designers at Astra, FermionIC and Signalchip tape out abroad.

WhatItBlocks: India's luxury market is barely 1% of 4.4 million annual car sales and has no domestic entrant. Tata owns Jaguar Land Rover, engineered in the UK.
RecursIn: Mercedes-Benz Group · BMW Group · Volkswagen Group · Brembo
CoreTechnology: Longitudinal premium platform with NVH and chassis calibration
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: A modular platform with air or adaptive suspension, a high-torsional-stiffness body, the electrical architecture behind it, and the noise, vibration and chassis calibration that is what premium actually means to a buyer.
WhyItIsHard: Calibration and durability validation accumulated across model generations, plus brand. Neither is a factory investment.
WhereIndiaStands: Tata Motors and Mahindra now build genuinely global-class SUVs and EV platforms, and JLR is Tata-owned and holds real premium platform IP. The Indian-originated premium platform is still the gap.

HeldBy: Mercedes MBRDI, BMW TechWorks, VW, Bosch, Continental in India
WhatItBlocks: India runs some of the largest automotive engineering centres in the world for foreign owners and holds none of the platform or software IP they produce.
RecursIn: Mercedes-Benz Group · BMW Group · Volkswagen Group · Bosch
CoreTechnology: Offshore engineering capacity without design authority
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: Not a technology gap but an ownership one. Mercedes, BMW, Volkswagen, Bosch and Continental run large Indian engineering centres whose output vests entirely abroad.
WhyItIsHard: Nothing technical whatsoever. Design authority is assigned by a board, not earned by a team.
WhereIndiaStands: India has the engineers, and Tata Elxsi, KPIT, LTTS and Cyient do the identical work as services. This one is purely decision.

WhatItBlocks: Measuring a part while the machine is still cutting it — the difference between making a precision part once and making it repeatably. Every precision gap in this ledger sits on top of it.
RecursIn: Marposs · Hexagon AB · Carl Zeiss · Fortive
CoreTechnology: Traceable contact probing and machine error-map compensation
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Touch and scanning probes resolving sub-micron with repeatable trigger force, plus ballbar and laser calibration artefacts and the software that maps a machine's volumetric errors and compensates them.
WhyItIsHard: Probe mechanics and traceable calibration, then being written into the machine builder's standard specification so the probe ships with the machine.
WhereIndiaStands: Accurate Gauging, Sipcon and Manatec build gauging and test equipment, and Micromatic and Ace Micromatic build the machines. Renishaw-class probing is the gap between them.

WhatItBlocks: India is the world's second-largest tile producer and Morbi's presses, kilns and digital decoration are all Italian.
CoreTechnology: Large-format continuous pressing and roller-kiln firing control
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Continuous belt presses forming slabs over 1.6 metres wide, then roller kilns whose firing curve is controlled along the length and across the width to hold flatness and colour, with digital inkjet decoration at the end.
WhyItIsHard: Pressing and kiln thermal control at large format. Sacmi and System Ceramics hold the installed base and the process recipes with it.
WhereIndiaStands: India is the world's second-largest tile producer, concentrated at Morbi, and buys Italian lines. Indian machine builders serve smaller formats well. Capital and decision.

WhatItBlocks: Harmonic and cycloidal reducers gate every industrial robot arm. Indian integrators import all of them.
CoreTechnology: Strain-wave and cycloidal reducer tooth geometry at zero backlash
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: A harmonic drive's flexspline tooth profile and elliptical wave generator giving a high ratio in one stage at near-zero backlash, or cycloidal reducers for the heavy first axes, with gears ground to single-digit arc-seconds.
WhyItIsHard: Tooth-profile intellectual property, then heat treatment and grinding repeatability at volume. Fatigue life over tens of millions of cycles is the proof a robot builder demands.
WhereIndiaStands: Shanthi Gears, Elecon, Precision Rings and NRB Bearings hold the gear and bearing base. Systemantics, Addverb and TAL build robots on imported reducers. The single clearest chokepoint under Indian robotics.

HeldBy: DMG Mori, Mazak, Makino, Okuma, Hermle, GROB
WhatItBlocks: Turbine blades, impellers, implants and airframe structures cannot be made without simultaneous five-axis machining, and the class is export-controlled for defence end-use. Ethereal Machines is the sole Indian builder.
RecursIn: DMG Mori · Walter group · GE Aerospace · Silmax
CoreTechnology: Simultaneous five-axis kinematics, thermal stability and the CNC core
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: A machine whose tilting rotary table or swivel head keeps the tool-centre point within microns while every axis moves at once, on a thermally stable casting, run by a controller doing look-ahead and kinematic transformation in real time.
WhyItIsHard: The controller, which is FANUC, Siemens or Heidenhain, the volumetric accuracy, and decades of casting and assembly practice that no drawing captures.
WhereIndiaStands: Jyoti CNC, Ace Micromatic, Electronica and LMW build three- and four-axis machines of real quality and some five-axis. The controller is always imported. Capital and technology, and narrowing.

HeldBy: IBAG, GMN, THK, HIWIN, NSK, Schaeffler
WhatItBlocks: Spindles, guideways and ballscrews go into every Indian-built machine tool and none are made in India — including inside Ethereal's five-axis machines.
RecursIn: DMG Mori · FANUC · Georg Fischer · SKF group
CoreTechnology: High-speed spindle bearing systems and preloaded recirculating guideways
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Motorised spindles running 24,000 to 60,000 rpm on hybrid ceramic or air bearings, balanced to fine grades and liquid cooled, plus linear guides and ballscrews whose preload and recirculation geometry hold stiffness over millions of cycles.
WhyItIsHard: Bearing quality, grinding, and assembly cleanliness. Life testing is the qualification and it takes as long as the life being claimed.
WhereIndiaStands: NRB Bearings, Rajratan and Precision Rings cover bearings and precision components. Indian machine builders import rails from THK and HIWIN and spindles from Europe. Capital and qualification.

HeldBy: Broadcom (~70% of the market), Marvell, Alchip, GUC
WhatItBlocks: Turning a hyperscaler's architecture into working silicon. It is how Google's TPUs and OpenAI's accelerators get built, and the alternative to buying NVIDIA. India sells design services into it and owns none of the silicon.
CoreTechnology: Hard IP portfolio and advanced-node tapeout execution
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: Turning a hyperscaler's architecture into silicon: HBM physical interfaces, 112 and 224 gigabit SerDes, die-to-die links, floorplanning at three to five nanometres, and advanced packaging — an IP portfolio plus execution.
WhyItIsHard: The hard IP portfolio and an allocation of advanced packaging capacity. Broadcom holds both, which is why it holds most of the market.
WhereIndiaStands: Indian design centres do exactly this work for foreign principals, and eInfochips, Sasken, SmartSoC, Ignitarium and Mistral have the skills. No Indian firm owns the hard IP.

WhatItBlocks: Routers and access points terminating one of the world's largest broadband subscriber bases, held almost entirely by Chinese and Taiwanese brands. VVDN builds them as an ODM for others.
CoreTechnology: Wi-Fi SoC firmware integration and RF certification at consumer cost
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: A router is a reference SoC, an RF front end, a tuned antenna and a firmware and interface stack certified per market, delivered at a bill of materials of a few dollars.
WhyItIsHard: Nothing exotic. The cost structure and the Chinese component supply chain behind it.
WhereIndiaStands: VVDN, Syrma, Dixon and SFO Technologies already manufacture routers and optical terminals for global brands, and Matrix Comsec and CP Plus hold Indian brands. Decision and channel.

WhatItBlocks: Radio and dispatch systems that police, fire and disaster response depend on when cellular fails. India builds military radios and imports the civil ones.
RecursIn: Motorola Solutions · Ericsson & Nokia · Leonardo · Thales
CoreTechnology: TETRA and P25 protocol stacks with mission-critical assurance
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: Narrowband trunked radio with sub-second call setup, direct mode, end-to-end encryption, and the dispatch and network management an agency certifies — now extending to mission-critical push-to-talk over LTE.
WhyItIsHard: The protocol stacks, the certification and the installed base. An agency replaces its radio fleet roughly once a generation.
WhereIndiaStands: BEL builds tactical and secure communications at genuine class, with HFCL, Tejas and Astra Microwave on radio hardware. Indian agencies still buy Motorola. Decision.

HeldBy: Arm (mobile and increasingly data centre), Intel and AMD (x86)
WhatItBlocks: Every device assembled in India carries a royalty on an architecture India does not own. Localising the factory does not touch it. RISC-V is the only mechanism that does.
CoreTechnology: Instruction set architecture plus compiler and binary ecosystem
TechnologyClassMeaning: Not a capability gap. A patent pool, a certification, a design authority or a distribution channel somebody else holds.
WhatItActuallyIs: The architecture is a specification. The value is the compiler backends, operating system ports, binary ecosystem and the verified microarchitectures that implement it.
WhyItIsHard: The ecosystem. RISC-V removes the licence barrier and leaves the software, verification and performance work standing.
WhereIndiaStands: India's strongest structural opening. IIT Madras Shakti, InCore, Mindgrove, C-DAC VEGA and Morphing Machines build RISC-V cores that actually ship. The gap is a high-performance core and the software around it.

HeldBy: PSMC, UMC and a small set of second-tier foundries; TSMC, Samsung and Intel do not license
WhatItBlocks: A country without its own node must license one. India's first commercial fab at Dholera runs on Powerchip process technology, which is why it is Tier C — Indian plant, Indian capital, foreign process.
CoreTechnology: Transferred process recipe without the yield-learning behind it
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: A licence delivers a process flow, a PDK and a tool list. It does not deliver the learning rate, the device engineers, or any right to develop the next node.
WhyItIsHard: The licensor keeps the know-how deliberately. A licensee stays a node or two behind permanently unless it funds its own device and integration teams from day one.
WhereIndiaStands: Tata Electronics licenses 28nm from PSMC, and others will follow the same route. The decision that matters is whether India funds process R&D alongside the fab or only the fab.

HeldBy: AUO (BHTC), LG Display, BOE, Continental, Visteon
WhatItBlocks: Qualified, long-life displays in every vehicle built. India assembles millions of cars a year and imports every panel and cockpit module in them.
CoreTechnology: Automotive-qualified panel with optical bonding and long-life reliability
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: Panels qualified for automotive temperature, vibration, sunlight readability and ten-year life, optically bonded to cover glass with driver and touch controller, integrated into a cockpit domain controller.
WhyItIsHard: The panel fab itself, then automotive qualification inside a seven-year programme cycle that no new supplier can shortcut.
WhereIndiaStands: No Indian panel fab of any kind. Vu, Dixon and Amber assemble modules, and Tata Elxsi and KPIT write the cockpit software. The panel is the hard gap.

HeldBy: Hoya, with AGC and Shin-Etsu supplying a minority
WhatItBlocks: The glass substrate every photomask is written on, held close to a monopoly by one Japanese firm. It sits upstream of ASML and of every advanced fab on earth.
RecursIn: Hoya Corporation · ASML · TSMC · Carl Zeiss
CoreTechnology: Defect-free Mo/Si multilayer deposition on ultra-low-expansion glass
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Forty to fifty alternating molybdenum and silicon layers, each a few nanometres, deposited on ultra-low-expansion glass flat to below a nanometre, with essentially zero phase defects across the whole imaging field.
WhyItIsHard: A single sub-nanometre bump prints on every wafer. Hoya's yield on this is arguably the narrowest chokepoint in the entire semiconductor chain.
WhereIndiaStands: None. Gold Plus Glass and Borosil make industrial and specialty glass, orders of magnitude away from this specification.

WhatItBlocks: Nearline and data centre storage depends on them and one supplier dominates. India assembles no drives and makes no substrates.
RecursIn: Hoya Corporation · Western Digital · Seagate · Amazon
CoreTechnology: Chemically strengthened aluminosilicate discs at nanometre flatness
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Thin glass discs lapped and polished to sub-nanometre roughness and a few microns of flatness, chemically strengthened so a head can fly nanometres above the surface at 7,200 rpm for years.
WhyItIsHard: Polish and cleanliness at that scale in volume. Glass is what allowed the thin discs that raised drive capacity, and one supplier holds it.
WhereIndiaStands: None. Gold Plus Glass and Borosil are architectural and laboratory grade.

WhatItBlocks: A thin fluoropolymer film inside every membrane-cell chlorine plant. India runs one of the world's largest chlor-alkali industries entirely on imported membrane.
CoreTechnology: Perfluorinated sulfonic and carboxylic bilayer membrane fabrication
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: A reinforced bilayer of perfluorosulfonic and perfluorocarboxylic polymer that passes sodium ions while blocking hydroxide, surviving years in hot caustic soda and chlorine.
WhyItIsHard: Fluoropolymer synthesis, bilayer lamination and reinforcement, and then a service life no plant manager will gamble on an unproven supplier.
WhereIndiaStands: Gujarat Alkalies, DCM Shriram and Grasim run very large chlor-alkali plants on imported membranes, while Gujarat Fluorochemicals and Navin Fluorine hold the fluoropolymer chemistry. Capital and qualification — a real opening.
