WhatItBlocks: Nothing joins optical fibre without one. India lays fibre at national scale and imports every splicer and consumable used to do it.
CoreTechnology: Core-alignment imaging with piezo alignment and arc calibration
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Two fibres imaged from orthogonal axes, cores aligned by piezo stages to sub-micron, then fused by an arc calibrated against ambient pressure and electrode wear, with splice loss under 0.02 dB estimated in the machine.
WhyItIsHard: The alignment mechanics, the imaging algorithm and the arc calibration. What is actually bought is reliability in a muddy trench.
WhereIndiaStands: STL, HFCL, Birla Cable and Aksh make fibre and cable at world scale and perform millions of splices a year on Fujikura and Sumitomo machines. A striking adjacency gap.

HeldBy: Fujikura, SuperPower, Shanghai Superconductor, THEVA, Faraday Factory
WhatItBlocks: REBCO tape is the enabling material for compact fusion magnets and next-generation MRI. India has magnet engineering and no tape production.
RecursIn: Fujikura · Philips · Vacuumschmelze · GE Vernova Hitachi
CoreTechnology: REBCO coated-conductor epitaxy on textured metal tape
TechnologyClassMeaning: A sequence of steps whose yield is learned, not specified. The recipe is the technology and it does not transfer with the equipment.
WhatItActuallyIs: A micron of rare-earth barium copper oxide grown epitaxially on a buffer stack on textured Hastelloy tape, kilometres long, with critical current uniform along the entire length.
WhyItIsHard: Epitaxy held uniform over kilometres. A single dropout destroys a magnet, and fusion and MRI demand is already outrunning world supply.
WhereIndiaStands: RRCAT, IUAC and ARCI do real superconductor research. There is no Indian tape production, while India builds fusion and accelerator programmes that will need it.

HeldBy: Toray, Hexcel, Mitsubishi Chemical, SGL, Solvay
WhatItBlocks: Export-controlled dual-use material. India was refused it and built its own precursor chemistry through NAL, DRDO and ISRO — capability that exists at programme scale and not at volume.
RecursIn: Toray Industries · Boeing · Airbus · GE Aerospace
CoreTechnology: PAN precursor spinning and intermediate-modulus carbonisation
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: A polyacrylonitrile precursor spun to controlled molecular orientation, oxidised and carbonised between 1,400 and 3,000 degrees to give intermediate and high-modulus fibre with a qualified, traceable strength distribution.
WhyItIsHard: The precursor is the technology, and the carbonisation line is a decade of know-how. Then aerospace qualification, which takes another decade. Export-controlled throughout.
WhereIndiaStands: Kemrock and HEG touch composites and graphite, and Reliance and Grasim hold the polymer base. No Indian aerospace-grade fibre; Tata Advanced Systems and Kemrock lay up imported prepreg.

WhatItBlocks: ADC and DAC resolution gates radar, test instruments, medical imaging and industrial control. Three firms hold the high-precision tier, and India designs instruments around imported parts.
RecursIn: Analog Devices · Texas Instruments · Fortive · Philips
CoreTechnology: High-resolution converter architecture with trimmed on-chip matching
TechnologyClassMeaning: Architecture and calibration accumulated over product generations. Reproducible in principle, expensive in engineer-years.
WhatItActuallyIs: 16 to 24 bit sigma-delta and gigasample pipeline and interleaved converters whose performance rests on component matching, chopping and per-die calibration trim on a mature specialty process.
WhyItIsHard: Analog design depth plus a stable in-house process the designer can rely on for twenty years. This is where Analog Devices' four decades actually sit.
WhereIndiaStands: FermionIC, Vervesemi, Signalchip and Netrasemi design real mixed-signal silicon — India's best semiconductor foothold. The precision converter class is still ahead of them.

HeldBy: Epson, Kyocera, Fujifilm Dimatix, Ricoh, Konica Minolta, Xaar
WhatItBlocks: The head inside every industrial inkjet — textile printing, ceramic tile decoration, packaging. India leads globally in textile printing volume and is second in tiles, and imports every head.
RecursIn: Seiko Epson · Sacmi · Fujifilm Holdings · Canon
CoreTechnology: MEMS piezo actuator arrays with stable drop formation
TechnologyClassMeaning: A machine or part held to a tolerance. Needs metrology, thermal control and assembly discipline more than novel science.
WhatItActuallyIs: Thousands of piezo-actuated chambers on a MEMS die firing picolitre drops at tens of kilohertz, with nozzle plates, ink-compatible materials and waveform control holding drop volume and placement stable across billions of firings.
WhyItIsHard: MEMS fabrication, fluid dynamics and materials compatibility together. Nozzle life is the product being sold.
WhereIndiaStands: Colorjet India and Negi Sign Systems build printers around Epson and Kyocera heads, and Jaysynth makes the inks. No Indian printhead.

HeldBy: Epson, Nihon Dempa Kogyo, Kyocera, Murata, TXC
WhatItBlocks: A crystal oscillator sits inside essentially every electronic product assembled in India. None are made here, and almost nobody names the dependency.
CoreTechnology: Synthetic quartz growth and photolithographic blank processing
TechnologyClassMeaning: A substance made to a purity, morphology or formulation nobody writes down. Chemistry plus decades of qualification.
WhatItActuallyIs: Hydrothermally grown cultured quartz, cut at precise crystallographic angles, lapped and photolithographically shaped to thickness tolerances that set frequency, then sealed and aged for parts-per-million stability.
WhyItIsHard: Quartz growth and angle and thickness control at volume. Temperature-compensated and oven-controlled oscillators add compensation circuitry and years of ageing data.
WhereIndiaStands: Deki Electronics and a few passive-component makers are adjacent. Essentially every crystal and oscillator in an Indian product is imported, and every product needs one.

HeldBy: Ansys (Synopsys), Dassault SIMULIA, Siemens Simcenter, Altair (Siemens), COMSOL, MathWorks
WhatItBlocks: Every Indian certification programme — aircraft, launcher, vehicle, bridge, chip — generates its evidence in licensed foreign software. India has one of the world's largest engineering workforces and two simulation product companies.
RecursIn: Dassault Systèmes · Synopsys · Siemens · Cadence Design Systems
CoreTechnology: Validated physics solvers with industry-correlated model libraries
TechnologyClassMeaning: Algorithms plus a validated model library plus an ecosystem that assumes it. The code is the small part.
WhatItActuallyIs: Finite-element and finite-volume solvers whose value is the validated model library behind them — turbulence closures, material cards, contact and failure models — correlated against decades of physical test and accepted by certification authorities.
WhyItIsHard: The solver mathematics is published. The correlation record and the regulatory acceptance are not, and they cannot be written in a release cycle.
WhereIndiaStands: Zeus Numerix, BosonQ Psi, Simyog and Cyient build genuine solver and simulation products. Indian industry runs on Ansys, Dassault and Siemens licences. India's strongest software opening.
